The abundance of solid HNCO is approximately estimated as 0.04--0.15\% relative to solid H$_2$O. The positive correlation between HNCO and N$_2$O suggests their co-formation via the chemical route that includes solid N$_2$. The results are also supported by the numerical modeling of HNCO formation in protostellar objects with predicted abundance of 0.06--0.11\%. We calculated the upper limits for CH$_3$CN toward two protostars and evaluated its abundance to solid water using the spectroscopic fitting and modeling.

entries.title: VVV CL001: A strong candidate for the most ancient star cluster in the Galaxy
entries.abstract: Finding the oldest globular cluster of the Galaxy is important to constrain a lower limit on the age of the Galaxy and the Universe. VVV CL001 ([l,b]= [5.26,0.77]) is perhaps the most metal-poor ([Fe/H]~-2.2 dex) globular cluster in the Galactic bulge and a promising candidate to be the oldest globular cluster in the entire Milky Way. Due to its recent discovery and high extinction, its physical parameters, especially the distance and age, remain highly uncertain, yet they are essential to define it as an ancient native stellar system of the Milky Way. We aim to refine the distance and age of VVV CL001 using deep and high-quality photometry, to study its role in the formation of the Milky Way, and to determine whether it is the oldest Galactic globular cluster. We used J and KS observations to construct the deepest CMD of VVV CL001 to date, based on FourStar/Baade PSF photometry combined with HST near-IR wide-filter PSF photometry. We selected cluster members through proper motion calculations and the HDBSCAN algorithm, and assigned membership probabilities via Markov-Chain Monte Carlo iterations in a 5-dimensional parameter space. Using r band data from DECam/Blanco, we optically identified horizontal branch members and applied an isochrone-fitting technique to determine the cluster distance, while members around the main-sequence turn-off yielded the age from different isochrone sets. Finally, we refined the cluster orbital parameters. We obtained a distance of d = 7.34 +- 0.46 kpc, the most precise to date. We derived an age of 13.4 +- 0.4 Gyr, indicating that VVV CL001 is one of the oldest globular clusters in the Galaxy. The orbit confirms that the cluster belongs to the Galactic bulge, which, together with its age and metallicity, could link it to the early proto-Milky Way assembly, extending the metal-poor end of the known in situ globular clusters.

entries.title: Understanding the formation of alpha-Fe bimodality in the Milky Way using constrained cosmological simulations of the Local Group
entries.abstract: We use a novel suite of constrained cosmological simulations of the Local Group to investigate the formation of alpha--Fe bimodalities in stellar discs of Milky Way analogues. In agreement with past studies using the Auriga model, we show that in our simulations the high-alpha sequence forms in a merger-induced starburst, which further quenches star formation, allowing the new stellar populations to form at low [alpha/Fe]. Producing a bimodality that is prominent at large radii, with a significant [alpha/Fe] gap and overlapping metallicity as in the Milky Way, requires the quenching of star formation across all radii where the bimodality is observed. The quenching can be achieved either with a galaxy-wide starburst, or with a retrograde merger reducing angular momentum in the outer disc and allowing more efficient dilution by the metal-poor gas in the circumgalactic medium (CGM). We show that mergers can also tilt the disc, changing the direction of galactic outflows and enriching a larger volume of the CGM with galactic metals, leading to low [alpha/Fe] scatter in the subsequently formed low-alpha sequence. We argue that the slopes in [alpha/Fe] of the two alpha sequences are crucial in narrowing down the mechanism that leads to their formation. We additionally uncover an indirect role that mergers play in enhancing the accretion of metal-poor gas onto galaxies. The smoothly accreted gas can dominate the gas content in the CGM and aid in the formation of distinct chemical sequences, especially at the low-metallicity end.

entries.title: Phakoseismology: Asteroseismology of gravitationally microlensed stars
entries.abstract: Asteroseismology relies on disk-integrated photometry or radial velocities, in which geometric cancellation suppresses modes of high spherical degree ($l\geq4$). Observations are thus limited to deeply penetrating, low-degree modes, leaving the outer envelope inaccessible. We investigate whether a high-magnification microlensing event can temporarily lift this limitation by differentially magnifying the surface of an oscillating source star. We modelled the visibility of solar-like oscillations during microlensing, weighting the surface by limb darkening and the local magnification. We computed multiplet visibilities and the power distribution among azimuthal components, and built a likelihood model for recovering the 3D spin-axis orientation from resolved rotational multiplets. When the lens-source separation becomes comparable to the source's angular radius, the magnification gradient acts as a transient spatial filter that breaks the symmetry of disk integration, raising high-degree mode visibilities by up to three orders of magnitude. The same non-axisymmetric weighting makes the relative power of azimuthal components depend on both the inclination and sky-projected azimuth of the spin axis, imprinting the full spin orientation onto the power spectrum. With $5\%$ relative-power uncertainties, we recover the orientation to $σ_i=2.9^\circ$ and $σ_γ=11.5^\circ$. Microlensing thus does more than amplify distant stars: its magnification pattern enables spatially selective asteroseismology. The effect is strongest for rare close encounters and unlikely to support large samples, and the newly visible high-degree modes will overlap with rotationally split and mixed modes, complicating mode identification. Nevertheless, individual high-quality events may open a window on envelope physics and spin geometries for stars in the Galactic bulge and beyond.

entries.title: Kinematically isolating intracluster light in AS1063: a distinct stellar population tracing the dark matter core
entries.abstract: We present a technique using integral-field spectroscopy to kinematically isolate intracluster light (ICL) from the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG), enabling insights into their contrasting stellar populations and the inner dark matter halo profile. Applying this technique to MUSE data of Abell S1063, we find that both components are old (~9 Gyr), but the ICL is more metal-poor than the BCG, implying distinct progenitor pathways. Within 100 kpc, the ICL comprises 55 per cent of the BCG+ICL stellar mass - substantially more than inferred from photometric decompositions. The BCG and ICL possess distinct velocity distributions, which remain nearly constant with radius, with an ICL velocity dispersion more than twice that of the BCG, and a line-of-sight velocity offset of 86 +- 18 km/s. Two-dimensional Sérsic fits yield an ICL centroid offset of 5.2 +- 1.5 kpc from the BCG. These phase-space offsets are indicative of the BCG oscillating in a broad potential minimum. Furthermore, the ICL surface-brightness profile matches that of strong-lensing estimates assuming a cored halo. Simulations indicate that the inner halo profile varies systematically for different dark matter models. Applied to larger samples, our method therefore offers a complementary route to testing the nature of dark matter, while simultaneously revealing the stellar origins of the ICL.

entries.title: Direct Urca process facilitated by non-Fermi-liquid quantum criticality
entries.abstract: Conventional Fermi-liquid theories of dense nuclear matter predict that the direct Urca process requires a proton fraction above a threshold of $Y_p \approx 0.11$--$0.15$, which is rarely reached in low-mass neutron stars. Here we show that this stringent kinematic constraint is drastically relaxed by the non-Fermi liquid behavior arising from superfluid and superconducting quantum criticality in neutron stars. In the non-Fermi-liquid regimes, nucleons have a smooth momentum occupation without a sharp Fermi surface, and their chemical potentials develop a logarithmic temperature dependence. These intrinsic features fundamentally alter the standard $β$-equilibrium relation. Consequently, direct Urca neutrino emission can be activated even at low nuclear densities. This modifies the long-standing Urca-threshold paradigm and indicates that direct Urca process has the opportunity to occur in low-mass neutron stars.

entries.title: Rapid Variability of Radiative Signatures from Driven Relativistic Reconnection
entries.abstract: Rapid variability in energetic flares is a distinctive feature of high-energy emission from many magnetically dominated astrophysical sources. We investigate the radiative variability of driven relativistic magnetic reconnection using Particle-in-Cell simulations of strongly magnetized flux tubes pushed to merge at driving speed $v_{\rm push}$. This setup captures the onset of reconnection and provides a controlled model for single reconnection-driven flares near compact objects, where magnetic structures can be twisted, sheared, and forced to merge by turbulent accretion flows or relativistic frame dragging. We find that the merger efficiently accelerates particles into nonthermal distributions, producing synchrotron emission whose variability tracks the reconnection phases. We identify two regimes: a quasi-steady, weakly driven regime for $v_{push}\leq0.1\,c$, and strongly driven regime for $v_{\rm push}>0.1\,c$. The transition occurs when the driving exceeds the typical inflow-to-outflow velocity ratio of $\sim0.1$ in steady collisionless relativistic reconnection, i.e., the average rate at which reconnection can process incoming flux, potentially providing an additional source of variability. The lightcurves rise on $1$--$3$ light-crossing times of the reconnecting region, and the particle spectra develop power laws with index $p\simeq1.8$--$2.4$. These timescales are compatible with observed variability in high-energy sources, including the very-high-energy flares of M87$^*$ and the $γ$-ray flares of the Crab Nebula, making this model a viable framework for rapid flaring in active galactic nuclei and pulsar wind nebulae.

entries.title: On the superbursts as photodisintegrators of ashes from the rp-process -- Numerical simulations of superbursts with MESA II
entries.abstract: Context: Superbursts are energetic explosions in the crusts of neutron stars in Low-Mass X-ray Binaries (LMXBs). At temperatures above 4 GK, photodisintegration of heavy rp-process ashes may play a major role alongside $^{12}$C fusion. Aims: We investigate how photodisintegration of rp-process ashes affects superburst properties and the initial $^{12}$C abundance required for ignition. Methods: We simulate superbursts with MESA v.24.08.1. Besides the canonical fuel of $20\%$ $^{12}$C and $80\%$ $^{56}$Fe, we test different $^{12}$C abundances mixed with scaled rp-process ashes. Results: Superbursts can ignite with only $10\%$ $^{12}$C when the remaining $90\%$ consists of rp-process ashes. Their luminosity is comparable to that of the canonical fuel, whereas $10\%$ $^{12}$C mixed with $90\%$ $^{56}$Fe yields lower luminosity. $^{56}$Fe remains the most abundant ash nuclide. Although photodisintegration drives nucleosynthesis, neutron, proton and alpha captures release energy at late times. We also find that $A=64$ nuclides or $^{20}$Ne help reduce the $^{12}$C abundance needed for ignition. Conclusions: The composition of accreted material - not just its $^{12}$C content - substantially affects superburst ignition, luminosity and nucleosynthesis.

entries.title: Constraints on Dark Matter Annihilation from Starlight-Induced Inverse Compton Emission in Omega Centauri
entries.abstract: The search for the particle identity of dark matter (DM) remains one of the foremost challenges in modern physics. In this work, we derive new constraints on the DM annihilation cross section $\langleσv\rangle$ by considering the inverse Compton (IC) scattering of DM annihilation injected $e^+e^-$ off the starlight radiation field in Omega Centauri. As a likely remnant core of a dwarf galaxy, Omega Centauri provides a dense stellar environment that enhances the predict IC signal. Using multi-wavelength observations from Chandra and Fermi-LAT, we establish upper limits on $\langleσv\rangle$ over a wide DM mass range from MeV to TeV. Notably, in the tens-of-MeV range, our results surpass existing constraints by approximately two orders of magnitude, exceeding $\langleσv\rangle \sim 10^{-31}~{\rm cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At several GeV to the TeV DM masses range, our constraints also remain stronger than existing limits. Our results demonstrate that starlight induced IC emission is an important component for indirect DM searches in dense stellar systems, establishing Omega Centauri as a powerful probe of the nature of DM.

entries.title: Pulsar J1909+0749 and Supernova Remnant G42.1-0.2: A case of a pulsar that has exited the shell of its associated supernova remnant
entries.abstract: (Abridged) The ATNF pulsar catalogue features only 63 pulsars that are possibly associated with a supernova remnant (SNR). Even rarer is the scenario in which the pulsar has escaped the physical extent of its corresponding SNR. We aim to identify the serendipitously discovered shell-type object G42.1-0.2 as a SNR. The known pulsar (PSR) J1909+0749 lies well outside the shell of SNR G42.1-0.2, but it has a cometary tail pointing towards the centre of the SNR; we propose that the SNR and the pulsar originated from the same supernova explosion. By measuring the flux densities of the shell G42.1-0.2 from ${\sim}$200 MHz to ${\sim}$6 GHz, we establish the nonthermal nature of its emission. With the characteristic age of the pulsar, its distance from the Sun estimated from the dispersion measure (DM), and the angular separation between the pulsar and the centre of the shell, we infer the evolutionary state of the SNR and the transverse velocity of the pulsar. Using proper motion measurements, we compare the SNR-pulsar direction with the velocity of the pulsar. The radio spectral index of the shell is $-0.36 \pm 0.08$, confirming that the emission is primarily nonthermal synchrotron. The proper motion measurements are not well constrained, but the amplitude and the direction are consistent with the interpretation that the SNR and the pulsar are associated. If the characteristic age and the DM-based distance represent the true age and the true distance of the pulsar and the SNR, then the standard evolution equations suggest that the SNR must still be in the Sedov-Taylor phase, evolving in a medium with a density of about 1.5 cm$^{-3}$. In addition, as a result of the PSR-SNR association, the transverse velocity of the pulsar PSR J1909+0749 is estimated to be ${\sim}1460~\mathrm{km\,s}^{-1}$, ranking it among the highest transverse velocities observed for pulsars in the Milky Way.

entries.title: Deriving Interplanetary Sector Boundary Crossings using Potential Field Source Surface Modeling
entries.abstract: The Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS) and associated interplanetary sector boundaries fundamentally structure the solar wind environment, modulating coronal mass ejection (CME) evolution and solar energetic particle transport. In this study, we evaluate the capability of a static Potential Field Source Surface (PFSS; $R_{ss}=2.5R_\odot$) coronal model to directly map interplanetary sector boundary crossings from the Sun to 1 au without dynamic heliospheric propagation models. We compare ballistically transported HCS crossings derived from GONG-ADAPT and SDO/HMI magnetic maps against sector boundary crossing observations from the SBCross catalog. PFSS modeling reproduces the large-scale interplanetary magnetic field topology well ($J\approx0.50$), achieving hit rates (POD) of 0.64 for GONG-ADAPT and 0.76 for HMI. Carrington synoptic maps outperform flux-transport modeled maps, suggesting that the short-term observational noise from data assimilation degrades topological matching more than map "aging". Predictive skill shows a strong solar cycle dependence, performing significantly better during solar maxima (POD=0.70-0.81) than solar minima (POD=0.56-0.67), attributed to more distinct crossings due to higher HCS inclination angles during maximum. Matched events exhibit travel times close to ballistic estimates of 4.8-4.9 days with an average timing difference centered near zero ($\pm1.1$ days) and 90% of events within $\pm 1.8$ days. The hit rate of HCS structures that interact with CMEs does not degrade (POD = 0.67-0.83), despite propagating $\approx7$ hours faster on average, implying that the CME interaction causes only minor structural changes to the HCS. Larger timing differences (>24 hours) are associated with flatter current sheets. Overall, static PFSS extrapolations offer a computationally inexpensive, effective approach for mapping global sector boundary structure.

entries.title: Detection and Statistics of large-scale Sector Boundary Crossings in the Solar Wind: The SBCross Catalog
entries.abstract: Heliospheric sector boundary crossings (SBCs), composed of the Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS), Heliospheric Plasma Sheet (HPS), and surrounding plasma halo, represent fundamental structures in the solar wind that influence interplanetary dynamics and space weather. We present the \textsc{SBCross} catalog, an automated, publicly available database containing 1,076 SBC events derived from in-situ observations spanning more than 30 years (1995--2026), covering Solar Cycles 23 and 24 alongside the rising and maximum phases of Solar Cycle 25. By combining interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) and 255~eV suprathermal electron pitch angle distributions (PAD) data, our algorithm reliably captures large-scale polarity transitions, with $76\%$ of detected SBCs exhibiting clear HPS signatures ($β> 1$, $n_{\mathrm{peak}} > 10\mathrm{\,cm^{-3}}$). Across the catalog, we find an average occurrence rate of $\approx 2.6$ events per Carrington rotation, a median event duration of $\approx 9.0$\,hours, and a median physical thickness of $\approx 7.4 \times 10^6$\,km. Furthermore, approximately $\approx 15\%$ of detected SBCs interact with interplanetary coronal mass ejections (CMEs) on average, with this proportion rising up to $33\%$ during solar maximum. These CME-associated events exhibit systematically longer durations (median of $10.0$\,hours), $54\%$ larger physical thicknesses, and higher average solar wind velocities. Notably, all high-velocity SBC events ($> 600\mathrm{\,km\,s^{-1}}$) are exclusively driven by CME interactions, demonstrating local plasma pile-up and structural entanglement resulting from fast CMEs overtaking the ambient slow background. The \textsc{SBCross} catalog serves as an updated successor to the classic SBC list by L. Svalgaard, delivering a standardized, open-access resource for the heliophysics community to systematically investigate sector boundary transitions.

entries.title: On the Stability of Tolman Oppenheimer Volkoff Fireholes
entries.abstract: We investigate the radial stability of singular Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff fireholes with a radiation equation of state. These configurations contain a naked, negative point-mass singularity surrounded by a positive-density fluid, whose mass profile develops a Schwarzschild-like plateau before approaching an extended, self-similar atmosphere. Using the Prüfer phase method to identify the fundamental radial mode, we consider two outer boundary conditions: vanishing Lagrangian pressure perturbation (open firehole) and vanishing radial displacement (boxed firehole). For both, the fundamental squared frequency changes from positive to negative as the outer boundary exceeds a critical radius $R_c$. We find that $R_c$ follows approximately the same scaling with the central mass parameter as the equilibrium firehole radius $R$. However, the stability thresholds differ significantly: $R_c^{\rm O}<R$ for the open firehole, whereas $R_c^{\rm B}\simeq R$ for the boxed one. The regular zero mode is the derivative of the equilibrium family with respect to the inner lapse normalization at fixed central mass. This gives the boxed threshold a turning-point interpretation and, together with a scaling symmetry of the TOV equations, implies $R_c^{\rm B}\to R$ in the limit of large central mass. Variational bounds show that the rigid wall is the most stabilizing separated, self-adjoint outer boundary condition and that the unbounded configuration is unstable. Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff fireholes are therefore radially unstable unless confined within approximately their firehole radius.

entries.title: Hidden engines in tidal disruption events: multimessenger signatures in a lepto-hadronic framework
entries.abstract: Tidal disruption events (TDEs) provide a unique laboratory for studying transient accretion, outflows, particle acceleration, and the possible connection between stellar disruptions and high-energy neutrinos. Motivated by recent candidate TDE-neutrino associations and by the forthcoming sensitivity of multimessenger facilities, we investigate under which physical conditions TDEs can be detected in MeV, GeV, and TeV gamma rays, and in high-energy neutrinos. We develop a lepto-hadronic emission framework and apply it to three representative sources: AT2019dsg, AT2019ehz, and ASASSN-14li. For each source we explore a set of physically motivated models that vary the proton and electron spectral indices, the minimum Lorentz factor of non-thermal protons, the particle energy partition, the acceleration efficiency, the magnetic compactness, and the presence of a compact corona. We compute the broadband spectral energy distributions, the associated muon-neutrino spectra, and compare them with reference sensitivities for COSI, Fermi/LAT, CTAO, and KM3NeT/ARCA. We find that hard proton spectra and/or large minimum proton Lorentz factors are the most favourable conditions for TeV gamma-ray and neutrino detectability, while GeV-bright models can be predominantly leptonic and neutrino quiet. AT2019dsg and AT2019ehz can reach the CTAO and KM3NeT benchmarks in hadronically favourable configurations, whereas ASASSN-14li is more naturally bright in the MeV-GeV band and constrained by its radio synchrotron emission. Our results highlight the importance of combining MeV, GeV, TeV, radio, and neutrino observations to distinguish between transparent, hidden, and lepton-dominated TDE emission regimes.

entries.title: Orbital Parameters for 65 Wide Binary Systems: no evidence for gravitational anomaly at low acceleration
entries.abstract: We use a Monte Carlo analysis to study whether wide binaries can be represented by bound Newtonian orbits, and, if this is the case, whether the distribution of the orbital parameters agrees with expectations. The potential orbits are classified according to the $χ^2$ probability of representing star coordinates, parallaxes, velocity components and masses. We apply this analysis to 44 systems previously published, to which we add 26 wide binaries, consisting of twin low-mass (M) stars. We find orbital solutions for 65 systems, and derive the distribution of their orbital parameters. For one system composed of M-type stars, no Newtonian bound solution can be found; however, this pair is a member of the young Argus association and therefore not a suitable target. The remaining four systems that cannot be fit were already identified as likely disrupted binaries. The uncertainty in the separation between the components, given by the parallax error, is by far the dominant error source, and the main limitation of the present analysis, affecting especially the determination of the orbits' inclination angle and phase. Newtonian dynamics describe well our sample. When dividing the sample into two subsamples, according to the mutual acceleration, the eccentricity and periastron distributions agree with theoretical expectations; inclination and phase are distorted by the parallax-limited separation, more strongly in the high-acceleration (37 systems) than in the low-acceleration ($A_N < 10^{-9} m s^{-2}$, 28 systems) subsample, which is opposite to what a gravitational signal would produce. In particular the ratio between observed velocity difference and circular velocity does not show any excess for the low acceleration sample. When parametrized as a boost $γ$ parameter to the velocity, $0.95 < γ<1.05 (1 σ)$, fully consistent with Newton also for the low acceleration sample.

entries.title: The Effect of Field Line Tracing Height on Wang-Sheeley-Arge Solar Wind Predictions at Earth
entries.abstract: (Abridged abstract): A key component of the widely used Wang-Sheeley-Arge model is the tracing of magnetic field lines in the solar corona, as that largely determines the modeled open/closed field regions and in turn the predicted large-scale solar wind structure. We demonstrate that by slightly raising the height from which magnetic field lines are traced from the photosphere (R$_{su}$), we can improve the prediction of solar wind high-speed enhancements (HSEs). We find a higher R$_{su}$ produces more accurate estimates of the HSE start time, duration, and peak speed, and enables the detection of HSEs that were missed with the standard R$_{su}$. These improvements are primarily associated with changes in the great-circle angular distance, while the flux tube expansion factors remain largely unchanged. A higher R$_{su}$ produces smoother open-field boundaries and reduces small-scale fragmentation within open-field regions. These morphological changes lead to more stable magnetic footpoint mappings and consequently more robust GCD calculations. To assess the statistical relevance of these findings, we extend the analysis to 53 Carrington rotations and perform a multi-metric evaluation of model performance. The results indicate that higher R$_{su}$ improves HSE predictions while reducing false alarms. We thus find that the choice of R$_{su}$ represents an important and previously underexplored parameter that can help enhance our ambient solar wind modeling and forecasting capabilities.

entries.title: Real-Time 24-hour Ahead Forecasting of Solar Energetic Particle Events with SEPNET-PRISM-R
entries.abstract: Solar energetic particle (SEP) events, operationally defined as proton flux exceeding 10 pfu in the >10 MeV channel, threaten spacecraft systems, astronaut safety, and high latitude aviation, yet continuous real-time forecasting with adequate lead time remains difficult. We present SEPNET-PRISM-R, a near-real-time system that issues hourly, 24 hour ahead probabilistic SEP forecasts. The model integrates multimodal solar data - including active region patches, flare features, coronal mass ejection (CME) characteristics, and historical proton flux - to concurrently predict SEP occurrences, peak proton flux, soft X-ray flux, and CME velocity, with the primary objective being SEP forecasting. Building on existing literature, SEPNET-PRISM-R enhances operational performance by incorporating a postprocessing module that enables cross-validated decision making and interpretable quantification of feature importance. The training dataset spans from February 1986 to September 2025, with subsequent forecasts generated sequentially through the present via a real-time space weather prediction platform that provides predictive probabilities, feature attributions, and historical analogs, enabling more reliable and informed operational decision-making. The proposed framework substantially suppresses false alarm rates while maintaining robust event detection capabilities, as evidenced by case studies and aggregate statistics.

entries.title: Coevolution of Dust Growth and Gravitational Instability in Massive Protostellar Disks
entries.abstract: Massive protostellar disks are expected to sustain high accretion rates through gravitational instability, while dust growth may modify their opacity, cooling efficiency, and stability. Conversely, the time-dependent and nonaxisymmetric structures produced by gravitational instability may regulate the local conditions for dust growth. However, the coupled evolution of dust growth and gravitational instability in massive protostellar disks has not yet been explored self-consistently. We present two-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations that follow gas dynamics, dust growth, and opacity-dependent radiative cooling in a massive protostellar disk. We find that dust grains rapidly grow to millimeter-centimeter sizes shortly after disk formation, substantially reducing the infrared opacity. The enhanced cooling promotes disk fragmentation and produces more frequent accretion-driven luminosity outbursts than in a model without dust growth, with durations and peak luminosities comparable to those observed in massive protostars. Dust growth is broadly regulated by the fragmentation-limited size in dense disk regions, whereas newly formed outer disk regions and low-density regions deviate from this limit because of finite collision timescales and dust transport. These results suggest that dust growth may facilitate episodic accretion and fragmentation, while gravitationally unstable disk structures in turn regulate the dust growth process.

entries.title: Data-Driven Ages from Asteroseismology for FGK Dwarfs
entries.abstract: Age is the one of the most difficult stellar properties to constrain. However, upcoming surveys such as PLATO are about to revolutionize our ability to measure FGK dwarf ages with asteroseismology. Here, we use The Cannon to construct a data-driven model for inferring asteroseismic-quality age measurements from large spectroscopic survey observations and demonstrate that forthcoming asteroseismology datasets from future surveys can be leveraged, together with our model, to obtain stellar age samples larger than can be obtained by those surveys alone. We train The Cannon on 323 FGK dwarf stars with asteroseismic age labels from NASA Kepler photometry and high-resolution spectra from the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE). We apply our model to FGK dwarfs from the Kepler survey that exhibit solar-like oscillations and reproduce their reported asteroseismic-quality ages with an RMS scatter of 1.0 Gyr. We then apply our model to the sample of 3810 Kepler FGK dwarfs with APOGEE spectra to infer data-driven asteroseismic ages. We repeat this for the larger sample of 48,828 FGK dwarfs with APOGEE spectra. Our work demonstrates that data-driven methods can robustly reproduce asteroseismic ages for FGK dwarfs. These methods will be invaluable tools for extending asteroseimology measurements from upcoming surveys (e.g., PLATO) to much larger stellar samples.

entries.title: Photometric variability of blue supergiants: Constraints on stellar masses and evolutionary stages
entries.abstract: Blue supergiants (BSGs) are crucial to understanding the evolution of massive stars. Although distinguishing between pre- and post-red supergiant (RSG) phases is challenging, stellar pulsations provide valuable constraints on their masses and evolutionary status. This study analyzes TESS light curves of six BSGs with high L/M to identify periodicities. We performed theoretical modeling of the radial unstable modes to characterize the strange modes. We aim to estimate asteroseismic masses, compare them with spectroscopic and evolutionary mass estimates, and assess the evolutionary stage of the stars. We employed the Lomb-Scargle periodogram and the weighted wavelet Z-transform to address quasiperiodic behavior and time-varying signals. A linear nonadiabatic stability analysis was performed to test for radial perturbations, generating eigenfrequencies that enable stellar mass estimation. In addition, we characterized the stochastic low-frequency variability (SLFV). We derive a first guess at the asteroseismic masses. We find that HD 74371 and HD 79186 are evolving blueward following the RSG phase, while the evolutionary stage of HD 115842 cannot be uniquely determined with the available mass estimates. We also find that HD 52382 and HD 99953 are likely in the post-RSG phase; however, their low masses are difficult to reconcile with the available evolutionary models. The extreme supergiant HD 80077 shows the largest mass discrepancy in the sample, suggesting a more complex evolutionary history. The SLFV properties do not provide a clear diagnostic of the evolutionary stage. These results highlight the potential of asteroseismology as a complementary tool for constraining the evolutionary status of BSGs. However, the mass discrepancies found for some objects indicate that additional observational and theoretical efforts are required.

entries.title: KMOS Spectroscopic Follow-up of 16 Star Cluster Candidates of the Sagittarius Dwarf Galaxy
entries.abstract: The Sagittarius (Sgr) dwarf spheroidal galaxy hosts several known globular clusters and numerous additional cluster candidates identified toward its crowded central regions. Establishing the nature of these candidates is difficult because apparent spatial and astrometric structure can arise from the underlying Sgr population. We investigate sixteen Minni stellar-cluster candidates with KMOS spectroscopy to determine whether the observed stars are compatible with Sgr and whether any candidate field shows evidence for a distinct stellar system. We analyse H-band KMOS spectra of 341 targets from the VVVX-GalCen Spectroscopic Survey, deriving radial velocities (RVs) and empirical metallicities. We compare these with an independent Sgr spectroscopic sample and use VVVX photometry and Gaia DR3 astrometry to test for localized stellar excesses relative to local control fields. Of the 341 KMOS targets, 256 (75%) have RVs within the adopted Sgr interval, and their metallicities broadly overlap the Sgr comparison population. No field shows statistically compelling kinematic evidence for a distinct system after accounting for the multiple candidates examined. Minni 329 shows the strongest spatial excess, but this is not significant after multiple-testing correction and is not accompanied by significant central concentration. The KMOS targets predominantly trace the Sgr population, but Sgr compatibility alone does not confirm the individual candidates as distinct stellar clusters. None of the sixteen fields can be confirmed as a separate stellar system with the present data, although this does not establish that the original candidates are spurious. Deeper imaging and larger spectroscopic samples are required to determine their physical nature.

entries.title: Hybrid Stars with Different Amount of Quark Matter
entries.abstract: In a previous work, we explored the possibility of neutron stars with large quark cores. Through Bayesian inference, we obtained large sets of equations of state imposing constraints regarding the properties of nuclear matter, mass-radius data from NICER, the GW170817 data from Virgo-LIGO collaboration, perturbative QCD and causality. We also imposed that the maximum mass neutron star (NS$\text{max}$) must have a large quark core. In this work, we obtain a new set of equations of state (SmallQ set) with the same constraints as before. However, we relaxed the last constraint, imposing only that NS$\text{max}$ must have quark core, regardless of its size. We compare the results with the set from our previous paper constrained by NICER and GW170817 observations NJL-GW. For both sets, we use the Relativistic Mean Field model with nonlinear meson interactions for the hadron phase and the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model with four- and eight-quark interaction terms for the quark phase. The SmallQ set has higher values of phase transition density, with 3 -- 4.5 $ρ_0$, compared to the NJL-GW, with 2 -- 2.5 $ρ_0$. The new set describes NSs with smaller radius and smaller tidal deformability, and is more compatible with NICER and GW170817 data. A difference in the quark matter composition is observed, with a larger quark strange fraction occurring in the SmallQ set. Within this set, $2 M_\odot$ NSs may contain little to no quark matter. It is shown that there is a non negligible fraction of EOS whose mass-radius curve presents a positive slope for 1.8 $M_\odot$ stars, while for nucleonic stars this fraction is negligible and for hyperonic stars the slope is always negative.

entries.title: Exponential Growth of Turbulent Cross Helicity in Shear-Flow-Driven Turbulence
entries.abstract: Cross helicity, the velocity--magnetic-field correlation, is an ideal invariant of incompressible magnetohydrodynamics and constrains energy cascades and magnetic-field generation. Although cross helicity typically decays via visco-resistive effects, we analytically demonstrate that it grows exponentially in sheared inhomogeneous turbulence. This cross-helical shear instability is confirmed using three-dimensional numerical simulations. Growth requires a nonzero gradient of the Reynolds--Maxwell stress to produce turbulent cross helicity; this production overcomes effective losses when shear exceeds a threshold set by the ratio of turbulent magnetic to momentum diffusivities.

entries.title: Identifying a jet-shaped point-symmetric morphology in the supernova remnant HB9
entries.abstract: I identify a point-symmetric morphology in the supernova remnant HB9 (G160.9+2.6), supposedly a core-collapse supernova (CCSN) remnant (CCSNR), and attribute this structure to two or more pairs of jets that exploded the star within the jittering-jets explosion mechanism (JJEM). The pairs of jets that shape the point-symmetric morphology of HB9 are part of a larger number of pairs that exploded the star. The point-symmetric structure is composed of a pair of ears, a pair of ears/nozzles, a pair of dents, and a pair of bright bars. Although these pairs of morphological features are small and the point-symmetric structure is subtle, I consider the identification robust. I use visual inspection to identify the point-symmetric morphology of HB9, a method commonly used to identify jet-shaped, point-symmetric morphologies in other astrophysical objects, such as cooling-flow clusters of galaxies and planetary nebulae. I present arguments for jet-driven shaping rather than CSM shaping. These findings support earlier claims that the JJEM is the primary explosion mechanism of CCSNe.

entries.title: Tight asteroseismic upper limits on hot subdwarf magnetism
entries.abstract: The apparent absence of magnetism in subdwarf B stars (sdBs) has emerged as an outstanding observational puzzle, especially in light of their likely origin in binary interactions. Gravity-mode pulsations in some sdBs offer a unique opportunity to extend recent successes in asteroseismic magnetic field detection in red giants. In the presence of strong magnetic fields, gravity modes are expected to be significantly damped, suppressing their observed amplitudes. We place stringent upper limits on magnetic fields in 30 hot subdwarfs by using the observation of low-frequency dipole and quadrupole modes to rule out magnetic suppression. Even under conservative assumptions, our upper limits constrain near-surface magnetic fields to below a kilogauss in roughly half of our sample, with the strongest individual constraint reaching down to $\sim20\,\mathrm{G}$. These upper limits reinforce the apparent dearth of magnetic fields in hot subdwarfs and demonstrate asteroseismology as a powerful new probe of magnetism in these stars.

entries.title: A Solar Optical Clock
entries.abstract: Precision spectroscopy underpins quantum sensing, atomic timekeeping, and the search for terrestrial-mass exoplanets. Finding an Earth-Sun analog requires fractional splitting of spectral features that rivals the precision of the best laboratory spectroscopy. This corresponds to resolution of a few parts in $10^5$ of a typical stellar spectral line, or a Doppler velocity precision of less than 10 cm s$^{-1}$. Only a few astrophysical spectrometers reach this regime, and only by dispersing starlight with large gratings and averaging thousands of lines. Here, we show that comparable precision can be achieved on a single solar line by leveraging techniques used in quantum sensors and optical clocks. A laser is frequency-locked to the 1565 nm solar Fe I line by coupling to a single mode of the solar thermal field and counted against an optical frequency comb referenced to the SI second, thus creating a solar optical clock. Operating at the fundamental photon-noise limit of thermal heterodyne spectroscopy, we achieve centroid precision of one part in $10^9$ of the optical frequency, or 30 cm s$^{-1}$ in radial velocity. We recover the Sun's five-minute acoustic oscillations and the expected Rossiter-McLaughlin signal during a solar eclipse. Combining these techniques from quantum sensing with a thirty-meter-class telescope could enable our demonstrated precision on the nearest Sun-like stars in a few hours. Multiplexing such absolute frequency measurements across lines with different magnetic sensitivity and formation depth would reduce averaging time and help disentangle stellar granulation and activity from the Doppler signature of terrestrial exoplanets, providing new approaches to address some of the most demanding measurements in astrophysical spectroscopy.

entries.title: Resonant three-mode coupling in asteroseismology I: Bifurcations, chaos, and DAV white-dwarf outbursts
entries.abstract: Resonant three-mode coupling is a fundamental nonlinear process in stellar oscillations and other wave systems. We investigate the global dynamics of a linearly overstable parent mode coupled to two damped daughter modes. The principal control parameters are frequency detuning $Δ$ and daughter damping rate $Γ$, normalized by the parent growth rate. We combine high-resolution maps of the largest Lyapunov exponent in the $(Γ,Δ)$ plane with linear stability analysis, Floquet calculations, and numerical continuation. The resulting parameter space includes stable equilibria, simple and period-doubled limit cycles, chaotic attractors, formally unbounded solutions, and higher-period `shrimp' islands within chaotic regions. Successive period doublings lead to chaos, while boundaries of isolated periodic windows exhibit type-I intermittency. At large $Γ$, the main bifurcation boundaries approach straight lines, indicating that the dynamics is governed primarily by $r=Δ/(2Γ)$. We connect finite-$Γ$ bifurcations to an earlier one-dimensional return map. As $ε\rightarrow0$, this map recovers the principal period-doubling sequence, the onset of chaos near $r\simeq0.38$, and the asymptotic positions of prominent periodic windows. We also examine the effects of unequal daughter damping rates. Applying these results to sporadic outbursts in cool DAV white dwarfs, we find that estimated $g$-mode growth rates, damping rates, and detunings place resonant triplets in both periodic and chaotic regimes. Thus, instability of the three-mode equilibrium need not produce a regular limit cycle: deterministic chaos and intermittency may contribute to irregular outburst amplitudes and recurrence times.

entries.title: The clumpy fraction of galaxies at $z=1-9$ with JADES: evidence for a mass-dependent transition in clump origin
entries.abstract: We measure the fraction of clumpy galaxies ($f_{\rm clumpy}$) over the redshift range $z=1-9$ and stellar masses $\log_{10}(M_\star/{\rm M_\odot}) \geq 8$ using JWST/NIRCam imaging from JADES. We define clumps as compact off-centre surface-brightness peaks with characteristic sizes of a few hundred parsecs, and develop a dendrogram-based clump-finding method with astrodendro to identify them directly in rest-frame UV, blue, and optical images. Clump-detection completeness is quantified through injection-recovery simulations, which we use to define ($M_\star$, $z$)-dependent 50 per cent completeness-limited $f_{\rm clumpy}$, alongside a probability-weighted completeness-corrected statistic for comparison. For the full sample, the blue and optical $f_{\rm clumpy}$ reach $\approx55$ per cent at $z\approx1-2$ and decline to $\lesssim5$ per cent by $z\approx8-9$, while the UV fraction remains higher at $\approx12$ per cent. At $z\approx1-2$, $f_{\rm clumpy}$ increases strongly with stellar mass, from $\approx35$ per cent in the lowest-mass bin to $\approx85$ per cent at $\log_{10}(M_\star/{\rm M_\odot})\geq10$. Most clumpy galaxies host only one or two robustly detected off-centre clumps, while higher-multiplicity systems occur preferentially in massive, strongly star-forming galaxies at low to intermediate redshift. Comparison with major merger rates suggests that mergers could account for a substantial fraction of low-mass ($\log_{10}(M_\star/{\rm M_\odot})<8.5$), high-redshift clumpy galaxies, while the observed fractions in more massive systems ($\log_{10}(M_\star/{\rm M_\odot})>9$) require an additional in situ clump-formation channel. Our results are consistent with a transition from merger-dominated clumpy morphologies at early times and low stellar masses to an increasing contribution from in situ clump-formation channels, such as disc instabilities, in more massive systems.

entries.title: A sub-Earth-sized TESS planet candidate in the nearby M-dwarf binary GJ 774, most likely orbiting GJ 774 A (TIC 351339274)
entries.abstract: Small planets transiting the nearest M dwarfs are the terrestrial planets most accessible to detailed characterisation. We report a sub-Earth-sized transiting planet candidate in the wide (17.6") M-dwarf binary GJ 774 at 12.86 pc, most likely orbiting the M2.5 primary GJ 774 A (TIC 351339274). The signal was a SPOC multi-sector threshold-crossing event (MES = 7.95) and is not a TESS Object of Interest. In eight TESS sectors (2019-2026) a 1.28-h transit recurs every 4.225138 +/- 0.000010 d with a box-mean depth of 365 +/- 32 ppm in A's light. The 2026 data, which entered neither the SPOC search nor our selection, show it at the ephemeris predicted from 2019-2023 data (304 +/- 43 ppm; none of 10^5 phase-scrambled versions of the 2026 data is as deep). The per-target false-alarm probability is < 0.03 at 95%. Odd/even, secondary-eclipse, archival-plate and Gaia radial-velocity tests exclude unrelated blended eclipsing binaries and eclipsing companions on 4.2-d orbits, and hierarchical eclipsing binaries are improbable. The stars are 0.85 TESS pixel apart, so the TRICERATOPS false-positive probability (0.26) is set by a planet on GJ 774 B. B is disfavoured because its own light does not dim enough: PRF-deblended photometry gives 109 +/- 115 ppm in B's light, against 1089 ppm required if B were the host. Conditional on a point source at A or at B, the joint host model gives P(A)=0.59-0.97 (0.97 for the native target-pixel baseline). Over all sectors the PRF photometry is consistent with A, but in the out-of-sample 2026 data 40% of the deficit appears at B's position, an unexplained 2-3 sigma (PSF-model and depth dependent) tension with host A. On A the planet has R_p=0.70 +/- 0.06 R_Earth, S=15.0 +/- 1.8 S_Earth and T_eq=548 +/- 16 K. It is not validated; resolved ground-based photometry of the pair would test host B directly.

entries.title: Large fluctuations and cusp-core transformation in dwarf galaxies
entries.abstract: Dwarf galaxies are abundant and dark matter dominated, rendering them particularly relevant for testing a cosmological model dominated by a dark sector. Whether their density profiles agree with $Λ$CDM expectations has long been a point of contention, dubbed the cusp/core problem. While numerical simulations have suggested that the erasure of central dark matter cusps may arise from potential fluctuations in feedback-driven gas, whether the required fluctuation levels are achieved in actual galaxies has remained uncertain. By measuring the power spectra of neutral gas density contrasts in a sample of gas-rich dwarf galaxies, we show that the observed fluctuations match theoretical expectations when their impact is derived from a stochastic dynamical model. Specifically, the relaxation times for core formation at the observationally estimated radii are generally on the order of a Hubble time or less. Core sizes are therefore consistent with conservative estimates assuming their generation through steady fluctuations acting over cosmic history. The relaxation time increases with halo mass, suggesting that core formation via this mechanism becomes less efficient in more massive systems.

entries.title: Resolving the extended interstellar medium of infrared galaxies II. Fine-structure line emission
entries.abstract: We investigate how star formation and active galactic nuclei (AGNs) shape the ionized and neutral interstellar medium in 67 nearby luminous and ultraluminous infrared galaxies from the Great Observatories All-sky LIRG Survey (GOALS). Combining mid-infrared (MIR) spectral mapping from the Spitzer Infrared Spectrograph with far-infrared (FIR) spectroscopy from the Herschel Photodetector Array Camera and Spectrometer, we measure fine-structure emission lines in aperture grids extending to projected galactocentric distances of about 14 kpc. We compare the measurements with CLOUDY photoionization models to constrain the ionization parameter, hydrogen density, stellar age, and metallicity. In starburst-dominated galaxies, the combined MIR+FIR fits yield a decreasing ionization parameter with radius, approximately constant hydrogen densities, uniformly young stellar populations, and flat metallicity profiles. MIR-only fits instead yield an increasing ionization parameter with radius, highlighting the importance of FIR diagnostics, particularly the [C II] emission associated with photodissociation regions, in constraining the multiphase gas. In the strongest AGN-dominated system, the nucleus and inner extended regions show elevated [Ne III]/[Ne II] and suppressed [C II]/[O I] ratios, while the outermost regions, at projected distances of about 6 kpc and beyond, show values typical of star-forming regions. This suggests that the AGN may affect gas excitation out to about 5 kpc. Our results demonstrate the importance of combining MIR and FIR diagnostics to recover radial trends that can be hidden in galaxy-integrated measurements. Together with Paper I, they provide a benchmark for spatially resolved studies of gas and dust in starbursts and AGN-hosting galaxies.

entries.title: Resolving the extended interstellar medium of infrared galaxies I. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon emission
entries.abstract: We investigate spatial variations in polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) properties and photoelectric heating efficiency in 67 nearby luminous infrared galaxies from the Great Observatories All-sky LIRG Survey (GOALS). Using mid-infrared spectroscopy from Spitzer and far-infrared cooling-line maps from Herschel, we extract spectra in concentric annuli and matched aperture grids out to about 14 kpc. PAH features are measured with the CAFE spectral decomposition tool. We trace photoelectric heating efficiency by combining PAH emission with cooling lines after isolating the neutral-gas contribution. In starburst galaxies, the PAH 11.3/7.7 ratio rises out to about 5 kpc while 6.2/7.7 remains nearly constant, indicating predominantly large, neutral PAHs. Between 5 and 8 kpc, 11.3/7.7 continues to rise while inferred PAH sizes decrease. Beyond 8 kpc, 11.3/7.7 falls and 6.2/7.7 rises, indicating smaller, more ionized PAHs. These trends are consistent with PAH photodestruction near the central starburst. Strong active galactic nucleus (AGN) systems show more neutral PAHs and harder radiation fields in their nuclear and inner regions. Beyond about 5 kpc, PAHs become more ionized and approach the starburst locus as the radiation field weakens. Strong AGNs influence average PAH charge states at 6-14 kpc as effectively as moderate AGNs at 1-6 kpc. Photoelectric heating efficiency increases with radius in both starburst and AGN-hosting galaxies as the radiation field weakens. In starbursts, higher efficiency is associated with more neutral PAHs, while AGN-dominated systems show the opposite relation. These results provide quantitative, spatially resolved constraints on the extent of AGN effects on dust properties in a population of luminous infrared galaxies.

entries.title: Automated optimization of solar energetic particle acceleration and transport parameters against five-spacecraft observations of the 9 October 2021 event
entries.abstract: Solar energetic particle (SEP) events threaten space infrastructure, yet physics-based prediction models depend on numerous poorly constrained free parameters. We introduce the Fujitsu Solar Energetic particle Intelligent Tuning and Evaluation Network (SEITEN), which couples the SUSANOO MHD model of CME propagation to SEPIF, a diffusive shock acceleration and focused transport model, through the shock conditions SUSANOO supplies, and automatically optimizes the free parameters of the particle model against the SEP event of 9 October 2021. The mean free path and the injection efficiency vary independently along each magnetic field line and heliolongitudinal bin, giving a 19-dimensional problem solved by quasi-Monte Carlo sampling followed by a Tree-structured Parzen Estimator. The optimized model reproduces proton flux profiles at five spacecraft with a mean absolute error of $\approx 0.45$ in $\log_{10}$ flux, and the inferred mean free paths show a clear east-west structure; these are effective parameters conditional on the assumed transport geometry. Six independent runs show that whether mean free paths or injection efficiencies dominate depends on the MHD shock strength, and that injection efficiencies differ by orders of magnitude between MHD configurations despite nearly identical fit quality. Joint MHD-SEP parameter estimation is therefore a necessary next step towards generalized, operational SEP forecasting.

entries.title: Dynamical stability of Magnetic Supramassive Neutron Stars
entries.abstract: We investigate the dynamical stability of strongly magnetized supramassive neutron stars close to the mass-shedding limit using fully general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations in three spatial dimensions. Equilibrium configurations are constructed using a microphysical equation of state and considering poloidal magnetic fields up to maximum strengths ${\sim} 10^{17}\,\mathrm{G}$. The initially unstable magnetic fields reorganize into mixed poloidal--toroidal configurations on Alfvén timescales shorter than the stellar rotation period. The subsequent dynamical evolution is governed by timescales set by the Lehnert number. For stars with masses sufficiently lower than the maximum mass, magnetic stresses redistribute angular momentum and drive the development of differential rotation, leading to a new quasi-stationary configuration that remains dynamically stable over several rotation periods. Magnetically-driven winds develop from the outer layers around the equatorial plane and remain baryon-matter dominated with magnetization ${\lesssim}0.2$. Over the simulated timescale, winds carry a total rest mass of order ${\sim}10^{-3}\mathrm{M}_\odot$ at outflow rates of up to a few $M_\odot/\mathrm{s}$. For stars close to (or beyond) the maximum-mass turning point along the stellar equilibrium sequence, strong magnetic fields trigger gravitational collapse by redistributing angular momentum away from the stellar core. The resulting black hole remnants are characterized by angular velocities up to ${\sim}49\%$ larger and angular momentum ${\lesssim}8\%$ smaller than those of the initial equilibrium stars. Our results show that extreme magnetic-field instabilities can significantly alter the structure of supramassive neutron stars, with possible implications for magnetars and long-lived binary neutron-star merger remnants.

entries.title: Constraints on Millimeter-wave Extragalactic Transient Populations from 4 Years of SPT-3G data
entries.abstract: Wide-field cosmic microwave background (CMB) instruments have reached sufficient sensitivity and cadence to conduct untargeted millimeter-wave searches for astronomical transients. To date, such searches have primarily discovered stellar flares, while extragalactic detections remain limited to a few flaring blazars and active galactic nuclei. In contrast, recent simulations suggest that current and future CMB experiments should detect a few to dozens of extragalactic transients per year from sources including gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), tidal disruption events, and fast blue optical transients. At timescales under one week, predicted detections are dominated by flares from reverse shocks in long-duration GRBs, with some benchmark models predicting rates of ~10 detections per year for the SPT-3G camera on the South Pole Telescope. In this work, we conduct a transient search optimized for the bright and brief millimeter-wave emission from GRB reverse shocks. We update previous simulations by incorporating a more realistic model of the SPT-3G sensitivity, observing cadence, and detection algorithm, resulting in nearly a factor of two improvement in detection sensitivity compared to prior estimates. We subsequently carry out a search over four seasons of the 1500 deg2 SPT-3G Main field observations from 2019-22, finding no candidate extragalactic events. We use the lack of detections to constrain the parameters of the synthesized GRB populations, setting upper limits on the fraction of GRBs with reverse shock components, f_RS, and the all-sky rate of reverse shocks beamed at Earth, N_all-sky. For a standard 10^51 erg GRB with Lorentz factor Gamma = 100, we constrain f_RS <0.57 and N_all-sky <1226 bursts/year (at 90% confidence). The most readily detectable model we consider is a 10^52 erg "dirty" GRB with Gamma = 50, whose population we constrain to f_RS <0.09 and N_all-sky <120 bursts/year.

analysis.title_zh: 天体物理与宇宙学中的图神经网络综述
analysis.reason: 本文是针对天体物理学与宇宙学中图神经网络（GNN）与几何深度学习的系统综述。文章不仅梳理了宇宙学大尺度结构、暗物质晕并合树、引力系统动力学以及仪器探测（如 IceCube 等中微子和宇宙线探测器的事例重建与光纤调度）中 GNN 的架构原理，还深入建立了平移/旋转等变性与消息传递机制的物理数学映射，对高能瞬变天体物理及相关中微子望远镜数据处理有重要方法学参考价值。
analysis.result:
系统阐释了 GNN 在天体物理非欧几何数据结构中的建模优势：(1) 在大尺度结构与星系巡天中，利用包含节点与边特征的宇宙图无似然推断直接提取非高斯统计信息，对宇宙学参数 $\Omega_m$ 与 $\sigma_8$ 的约束优于标准 N 点关联函数；(2) 单步消息传递机制的物理本质等价于可学习的广义相互作用力定律加单步积分器，其单步计算复杂度由边数、节点数和隐藏层维度主导：$N_\mathrm{total} \sim N_\mathrm{E} N_\mathrm{lat} N_\mathrm{hid} \sim N_\mathrm{V} \langle k angle N_\mathrm{lat} N_\mathrm{hid}$；(3) 针对中微子望远镜（IceCube 等）和宇宙线探测器的不规则阵列重建，引入光锥因果连边条件 $A_{ij}=1	ext{ if }d_{ij}\le c\cdot(t_j-t_i)$，在精度与运行速度上显著超越传统似然重建；(4) 指明了求和（sum）聚合相较于均值（mean）能更完备保留局部密度等物理量，并揭示了多体相互作用消息（如 MACE 架构扩展至 $
u+1$ 阶 $\sum_{j_1<\dots<j_
u}\psi(\mathbf{x}_i,\mathbf{x}_{j_1},\dots,\mathbf{x}_{j_
u})$）对抑制过平滑（oversmoothing）与过挤压（over-squashing）的作用。
analysis.problem: 常规欧几里得网格架构（如标准 CNN）无法原生适配天体物理中高度非规则、稀疏的点云分布、层次化因果拓扑（如并合树）以及不规则探测器阵列（如中微子天文台）；传统统计量（如功率谱与 N 点关联函数）在非线性演化尺度上存在严重的信息损失且受制于尺度截断，需引入符合几何对称性（平移、旋转与置换群）的深度学习归纳偏置。
analysis.method: 基于几何深度学习蓝图（堆叠 $G$-等变层 $B$、非线性 $\sigma$、局部池化 $P$ 及全局不变量池化 $A$）：$$f = A \circ \sigma_J \circ B_J \circ P_{J-1}\circ\cdots\circ P_1 \circ \sigma_1 \circ B_1$$在图结构 $G=(V, E, U)$ 上建立广义消息传递层：$$\mathbf{h}_i = \phi\left(\mathbf{x}_i, \bigoplus_{j\in\mathcal{N}(i)} \psi(\mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j, \mathbf{e}_{ij})\right)$$类比引力 $N$ 体速度积分更新 $\mathbf{v}_i^{t+1} = \mathbf{v}_i^{t} + \Delta t \sum_{j\neq i} \frac{G m_j(\mathbf{x}_j^t-\mathbf{x}_i^t)}{|\mathbf{x}_j^t-\mathbf{x}_i^t|^3}$；证明了平移等变性下线性算符必然等价于循环矩阵与卷积 $(\mathbf{W}\mathbf{x})[m] = (\mathbf{w}\ast\mathbf{x})[m]$；构建兼顾置换等变性（节点/边层级）与置换不变性（整图层级预测）的网络拓扑。
assumptions: 输入物理系统在空间变换群（如欧几里得群 $E(3)$、$SE(3)$ 或置换群 $\Sigma_n$）下满足严格或近似的函数不变性（$f(g.x) = f(x)$）或等变性（$f(g.x) = g.f(x)$）
天体物理图的节点带有质量、速度、坐标等丰富的连续物理特征向量，突破了计算机科学中纯拓扑 Weisfeiler--Lehman (WL) 测试的表达力瓶颈
limits: 深层图神经网络易受邻域消息传递导致的过平滑（特征趋同热化）与过挤压（长程信息在瓶颈边受损）效应限制，实际应用中层数通常局限于 2 至 3 层

analysis.title_zh: Gaia BH3 光致电离气体的光学与紫外发射：档案数据限制与 2029 年近星点预测
analysis.reason: 该工作聚焦休眠恒星级黑洞 Gaia BH3 的星风吸积与光致电离机制，结合 Chandra X 射线限制与 ESPRESSO/UVES 高分辨率光谱，精确模拟了吸积流非平衡平流效应与宽发射线轮廓，对致密天体高能观测与环境光电离建模具有参考价值。
analysis.result: 研究给出 Chandra X 射线远星点上限限制氢电离光子产生率 $Q(\mathrm{H}) < 1.8 \times 10^{40}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$（对应 ADAF 吸积率 $f_{\rm Edd} < 7.6 \times 10^{-7}$）。在低于 Chandra 限制时，近星点经非平衡平流修正后的最高 $\mathrm{H\alpha}$ 等效宽度仅为 $\mathrm{EW}(\mathrm{H\alpha}) = 3.4 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{\AA}$。慢星风模型下，Chandra 限制要求辐射吸积效率从 $\epsilon \lesssim 0.2$（当 $\dot{M}_{\rm w}=10^{-11}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$）降至 $\epsilon \lesssim 2 \times 10^{-4}$（当 $\dot{M}_{\rm w}=10^{-8}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$）；档案光谱进一步独立排除了 $\dot{M}_{\rm w} \ge 2 \times 10^{-9}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ 且 $\epsilon \ge 3 \times 10^{-3}$ 的参数区间。
analysis.problem: Gaia BH3 在远星点的 Chandra X 射线光度上限仅能对吸积功率施加简并约束，无法独立解耦伴星巨星的星风质量损失率 $\dot{M}_{\rm w}$ 与黑洞捕获吸积效率 $\epsilon$；同时内流气体的快速平流下落和多普勒展宽会剧烈削弱光学窄发射线的可观测强度。
analysis.method: 构建包含慢风（$v_\infty = 30\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$）和快风（$v_\infty = 100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$）的 $\beta$ 律星风吸积动力学模型，采用 ADAF 谱作为中心源，通过沿 17–19 条视线求解 1D Cloudy 光致电离，并联立稳态平流动力学方程 $v \frac{dx_i}{dl} = \mathcal{I}_i - \mathcal{R}_i$ 与能量方程进行非平衡复合与绝热压缩加热修正；最后基于 UVES 和 ESPRESSO 档案光谱采用单边截断统计量 $\Delta\chi^2$ 约束谱线振幅并预测 2029 年近星点测验方案。
assumptions: 慢星风假定捕获半径受限于轨道间距（$R_{\rm acc}=r$），且吸积截获份额固定为 25%
limits: 当电离光子率 $Q(\mathrm{H}) < \dot{N}$ 时，吸积流保持中性，自由落体尖点产生的 $\mathrm{H\alpha}$ 展宽高达数千 $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ 导致光学窄线无法探测
低于 Chandra 观测限时慢星风光学线在近星点无法被现有高分辨率光谱仪直接检出，需转向紫外共振吸收线观测
citation_leads: Theoretical Model: “For the slow wind $2GM_{\rm BH}/v_{\rm rel}^2$ is 44~AU at apastron and 4.6~AU at periastron, larger than the separation at every phase: the wind is bound to the BH from the moment it leaves the giant”
Data and Methods: “The statistic measures how many sigmas the fitted amplitude falls short of the prediction.”
Results: “Gas inside the accretion radius moves with the BH as it falls toward it, so that its emission forms a cusp at the BH velocity, with wings extending to thousands of \kms.”
Results: “Below the Chandra bound the brightest corrected periastron EW(H$\alpha$) is $3.4\times10^{-3}$~\AA, against $5.3\times10^{-3}$~\AA\ in equilibrium.”
analysis.research_progress: 建立了考虑气体下落非平衡复合平流与绝热压缩效应的黑洞星风光电离线型计算方法，给出了 Gaia BH3 在轨道不同相位的发射线等效宽度与轮廓演化预测，并首次利用档案光学高分辨率光谱给出了伴星星风质量损失率与吸积效率的联合排除界限。

analysis.title_zh: 利用爱因斯坦望远镜定位双中子星：三角形与双L构型的全贝叶斯对比
analysis.reason: 该工作针对下一代引力波望远镜爱因斯坦望远镜（ET）的选址与几何构型争论（单址三角形 $\Delta$ vs 双址 2L），通过高阶模与地球自转效应的全贝叶斯参数估计，直接给出了双中子星（BNS）天区定位能力的定量对比，这对未来千新星（KN）及短 GRB 的多信使电磁后随观测策略具有关键指导意义。
analysis.result: 对于占主体的中低信噪比事件（$\mathrm{SNR} < 100$），$\Delta$ 构型由于天线响应简并，天区后验会裂解为 8 个离散模式，其 $90\%$ 可信天区面积 $\Delta\Omega_{90\%}$ 可达 $\sim 2 \times 10^4\ \mathrm{deg}^2$，真实位置仅占 $\sim 10\%$ 概率；而 2L 构型能有效打破简并，天区聚焦于包含 $\ge 50\%$ 概率的单一主导模式，$\Delta\Omega_{90\%}$ 缩小 1 到 2 个数量级（例如降至 $80 \sim 470\ \mathrm{deg}^2$）。仅在极高信噪比（$\mathrm{SNR} \sim 500$）或近距源（$D_L \sim 40\ \mathrm{Mpc}$）下，$\Delta$ 构型方可依靠分辨基线间亚毫秒到达时延 $\Delta t$ 消除多峰简并。
analysis.problem: 爱因斯坦望远镜（ET）在单址 10 km 三角形（$\Delta$）与两台分立 15 km 探测器（2L）构型下，对真实双中子星（BNS）并合引力波事件的天区定位精度存在未知差异；传统 Fisher 矩阵近似无法准确捕捉非高斯天区多峰简并，亟需在计入地球自转、高阶辐射多极矩与长波长近似失效的全贝叶斯框架下进行评估。
analysis.method: 采用结合高阶模式（HOMs，如 $(\ell, |m|) = (2,|1|), (3,|3|), (3,|2|), (4,|4|)$）与逐模相对分箱（relative binning）技术的贝叶斯参数估计框架（{\sc Bilby-xg} 与流匹配采样器 {\sc nessai}）；计入地球自转多普勒频移 $\Delta t = \hat{n} \cdot \mathbf{d}/c$ 和频率相关天线响应，在 $f_\mathrm{min} = 6\ \mathrm{Hz}$（设计灵敏度对比为 $3\ \mathrm{Hz}$）至 $4096\ \mathrm{Hz}$ 频段，对光度距离 $40 \sim 2000\ \mathrm{Mpc}$ 的注入事件系统对比 EMR 选址的 $\Delta$ 与撒丁岛-卢萨蒂亚 2L 构型。

analysis.title_zh: XMM-Newton EPIC-MOS2 25年非聚焦粒子背景：太阳活动周调制、银河宇宙线关联及其对 NewAthena 的启示
analysis.reason: 该工作利用 XMM-Newton EPIC-MOS2 积累 25 年的视场外数据，系统量化了空间 X 射线探测器非聚焦粒子背景随 11 年太阳周期、22 年 Hale 磁极性周期及 $\sim 27\,\mathrm{day}$ 太阳自转调制的演化规律，并与 AMS-02 和 Chandra ACIS 数据建立了精确的标度对应关系（相对本征弥散仅 $1.1\% \pm 0.1\%$），对高能瞬变源观测（如 X 射线暂现源、超新星及致密天体高能连续谱分析）的数据本底扣除和未来空间 X 射线巡天（NewAthena）的本底建模具有重要参考价值。
analysis.result: MOS2 视场外（outFOV）粒子计数率主要由能量 $E \gtrsim 100\,\mathrm{MeV}$（主要是 $0.4\text{--}1.2\,\mathrm{GeV}$）的高能银河宇宙线（GCR）质子诱发，在长时标上受 11.28 年太阳活动周及 $\sim 22\,\mathrm{yr}$ Hale 周期调制（在磁极性 $A>0$ 呈平顶而在 $A<0$ 呈尖峰轮廓）。MOS2 outFOV 计数率与 AMS-02 质子通量在 27 天并合尺度下表现出极强的贝叶斯线性相关 $Y = \alpha + \beta X + \epsilon$，相对本征弥散仅为 $1.1\% \pm 0.1\%$（RMSD 上限为 $1.34\%$）；与 Chandra ACIS 剔除率的相对本征弥散为 $2.25\% \pm 0.04\%$，且二者在日时标上无显著时延（峰值相关系数 $r=0.95$）。在太阳极大期探测到显著的 $\sim 27\,\mathrm{day}$ 准周期调制，线性拟合截距揭示存在约为 $(0.68\text{--}1.2) \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{cts\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}\,keV^{-1}}$ 的恒定非粒子组分，可能源自宇宙 X 射线背景（CXB）在探测器周围结构中的康普顿散射。
analysis.problem: 空间 X 射线天文望远镜的非聚焦粒子背景受银河宇宙线及其在日球层内的调制影响存在复杂的长短周期时变；如何精确评估其内在弥散、延迟及演化周期性，以满足未来下一代大口径 X 射线望远镜（如 NewAthena）对仪器本底建模精度达到 $\sim 2\%$ 的严苛要求。
analysis.method: 处理 XMM-Newton MOS2 探测器 2000 至 2025 年间 6718 次曝光（$\sim 222\,\mathrm{Ms}$，4744 圈轨道）的视场外数据，剔除辐射带（轨道相位 $> 0.8$）及太阳高能粒子（SEP）事件污染，重归一化至全探测器面积；采用贝叶斯线性回归拟合 $Y = \alpha + \beta X + \epsilon$ 量化其与 Chandra ACIS 和 AMS-02（质子刚度 $1\text{--}1.92\,\mathrm{GV}$）的内禀散射；结合 Lomb-Scargle 周期图、结构函数以及小波分析检验长短时标周期性。
assumptions: MOS2 视场外（outFOV）区域可有效表征探测器所处的高能非聚焦带电粒子背景环境
limits: 仪器本底依赖于宇宙线与航天器及探测器结构的相互作用，仅依靠外部粒子监测器无法完全替代原位测量与 Geant4 模拟

analysis.title_zh: 数值激波增宽与超新星中微子味转换：对 DUNE 的观测影响
analysis.reason: 文章系统研究了三维超新星数值模拟中网格展宽（激波被人为抹平覆盖数个网格）对中微子穿过 MSW H 共振区时非绝热味转换的虚假抑制效应，提出了激波前沿陡峭重构方案，并量化了该效应在 DUNE 等下一代探测器中的探测偏差与湍流微扰标度律，对超新星中心引擎与中微子信号建模具有重要参考价值。
analysis.result: 原始三维模拟网格将物理上极薄的激波虚假增宽至约 $1.63\sim1.67$ 个网格（$235\sim312\,\mathrm{km}$），达到振荡长度的 $3.5\sim4.7\,L_{\mathrm{osc}}$，人为诱发绝热演化；经波前锐化重构后，跃迁几率 $P_H$ 绝对值显著提升 $0.44\sim0.76$（中位数 $0.56$），且与突变极限公式 $P_H = \sin^2(\theta_m^- - \theta_m^+)$ 吻合极佳（相关系数 $0.9987$）。该效应使 DUNE 探测器在 $10\,\mathrm{kpc}$ 处的 $\nu_e$ 荷电流事件计数修正约 $-4.4\%$，泊松区分度为 $S=1.6$（在 $2\,\mathrm{kpc}$ 处增至 $13$）。附录揭示湍流诱导味转换泄漏量在弱扰动区服从二次标度律 $R \propto \sigma^{2.02\pm0.03}$，单模响应按波长 $\lambda^{1.4\pm0.1}$ 衰减。
analysis.problem: 核心物理与数值矛盾在于：真实超新星激波宽度由辐射介导且理论上仅毫米级，中微子穿过时应经历强非绝热突变跃迁；但流体动力学模拟中网格数值致宽使激波前沿覆盖数个网格（数百公里），导致波前宽度大于中微子共振振荡长度 $L_{\mathrm{osc}}^{\mathrm{res}} = \frac{4\pi E}{\Delta m^2_{31} \sin 2\theta_{13}}$，从而人为诱发非物理的绝热演化，严重低估跃迁几率 $P_H$ 并扭曲地球探测器的中微子计数预测。
analysis.method: 利用自研切比雪夫展开中微子味演化求解器 GHOST，在 Garching 数据库 6 个蓝超巨星 3D 爆炸模型（如 M15-7b）的单射线与角平均剖面中进行三味相干演化计算。采用双曲正切函数对数值平滑激波进行物理锐化重构（宽度由几百公里压缩至 $w \lesssim 2.2\,\mathrm{km}$）。结合 SNOwGLoBES 与 Nakazato 辐射模型计算 DUNE 探测器的 $\nu_e$ 事件计数；在附录中解析和数值研究了弱湍流密度场 $\rho(r) = \bar\rho(r)[1+\delta(r)]$ 引起的受激跃迁响应标度。
assumptions: 物质势计算采用中子质量 $m_n$ 约定
limits: 提高网格存储剖面的积分容差只能收敛到平滑斜坡的解，无法替代激波前沿的物理重构

analysis.title_zh: 双星星族合成中大质量主序星演化（二）：对黑洞大质量X射线双星与双黑洞的影响
analysis.reason: 该工作通过在快速星族合成中自洽追踪主序阶段对流核与富氦层演化，系统修正了黑洞大质量X射线双星（BH-HMXB）与双黑洞（BBH）并合通道的物理图像，为致密双星形成、引力波源质量比分布及致密天体高能吸积观测提供了直接的理论演化约束。
analysis.result: 采用自洽追踪对流核的 \texttt{BRCEK} 框架后，主序剥离星保留了更大氦核，成功形成传统 \texttt{HURLEY} 处方无法复现的 BH-HMXB；对于双黑洞并合，稳定物质转移（SMT）占 BBH 系统的 60%–80%（其中 Case A 占近半数），局部 BBH 并合率由传统模型的 $\mathcal{R}_{\rm HURLEY} = (10\pm1)\;\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ 提升至 $\mathcal{R}_{\rm BRCEK} = (33\pm2)\;\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$（与 GWTC-5.0 报告的 $27.5\text{--}49.4\;\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ 一致）；在 BBH 质量比分布上，Case A 物质转移显著抑制了剥离星的过度膨胀，使得探测到的 BBH 质量比峰值从原有的 $q \approx 0.7$ 显著移向近等质量比 $q \approx 1$。
analysis.problem: 大质量双星在主序（MS）核氢燃烧阶段发生 Case A 物质转移或星风剥离时，传统快速星族合成框架（如 HURLEY）依据零龄/终龄主序总质量粗略估算氦核，导致剥离星氦核质量偏小、无法解释 Cyg X-1 等高黑洞质量 BH-HMXB，且在双黑洞并合率与质量比 $q=M_2/M_1$ 统计分布上与引力波观测存在偏差。
analysis.method: 利用快速双星星族合成代码 \textsc{COMPAS}（v03.29.03），采用能够追踪任意传质历史下对流核演化、中心氦丰度及 CNO 加工轮廓的 \texttt{BRCEK} 框架；物质转移受吸积体热时标限制 $\beta_\mathrm{thermal} = \min \left( 10\times\frac{M_\mathrm{accretor}}{\dot M_\mathrm{donor}\:\tau_\mathrm{accretor}}, \:1 \right)$，多余质量按吸积体比角动量非守恒流失；计算 BBH 啁啾质量 $\mathcal{M}_\mathrm{chirp} = (M_1 M_2)^{3/5} / (M_1+M_2)^{1/5}$ 与 Bondi-Hoyle 风吸积 X 射线光度 $L_\mathrm{X} = \eta \dot{M}_\mathrm{acc} c^2$（$\eta=0.1$）。
citation_leads: Introduction: “In a massive binary system, interactions during the main-sequence (MS) phase, while the stars are still core-hydrogen burning, strongly influence the binary's subsequent evolution”
Results: “The case A mass transfer channel corresponds to systems in which the BH progenitor initiates mass transfer while still on the MS.”

Results: “Under \texttt{BRCEK}, the case A channel instead makes a significant contribution to the detectable population, and the overall distribution shows a strong preference for near-equal mass ratios.”

Conclusion: “This shifts the predicted population away from the previously reported mass-ratio peak at $q\approx0.7$ and toward $q \approx1$, in better agreement with the most recent gravitational-wave population results from GWTC-5.0.”
analysis.research_progress: 揭示了大质量主序星核反应区与对流核演化的精确追踪对双致密天体形成通道的决定性作用：证实了高度非守恒的 Case A 物质转移可有效解释 BH-HMXB 的短轨道周期与伴星氦增丰，并将引力波 BBH 并合群体的理论质量比分布定标为偏好 $q \approx 1$，消除了以往快速星族模型与 GWTC-5.0 观测分布的显著张力。

analysis.title_zh: 利用中子星并合引力波观测探测QCD相变的存在及其阶数
analysis.reason: 文章构建了包含无相变、一阶、二阶及三阶相变的庞大中子星状态方程参数库，并通过贝叶斯推断定量评估当前及未来地面引力波探测器（A+、A$^\sharp$、Cosmic Explorer）对星核超核物质向夸克物质相变阶数的甄别能力，对高能致密天体中心引擎及物态物理研究具有重要参考价值。
analysis.result: 对于 Cosmic Explorer 单个强事件（$\mathrm{SNR}=418$），一阶相变模型后验概率可达 $p(m=1|d)=0.74$，贝叶斯因子 $\mathcal{B}_{1/\rm none}=12.8$；在 $\mathrm{A}^+$ 与 $\mathrm{A^\sharp}$ 网络中，若真实物态存在低转变密度的一阶相变，累积约 14 次中子星并合事件即可达到 $p(m=1)>0.9$，并可测量密度跳跃比 $n_q/n_h$；但二阶、三阶与无相变模型易相互混淆，较难仅凭旋进阶段潮汐形变明确区分。
analysis.problem: 如何仅通过双中子星并合旋进阶段发射的引力波潮汐形变信号，定量检验中子星核深处是否存在夸克解禁闭相变并确定相变的具体阶数（一阶、二阶或三阶）。
analysis.method: 以 SK272 为强子相基底状态方程，通过构建重子密度比 $n_q/n_h$、相变起始密度 $n_h$ 及声速过渡剖面 $c_s^2(\epsilon)=1/3+(c_{s,\rm peak}^2-1/3)\operatorname{sech}^2[(\epsilon-\epsilon_q)/\Delta]$ 生成各阶候选物态方程参数网格，施加 $M_{\rm TOV} \ge 2.0\,M_\odot$ 与 $c_s \le 1$ 约束；解 TOV 和微扰方程计算潮汐形变 $\Lambda=\frac{2}{3}k_2(c^2 R/GM)^5$，结合高斯核重要性抽样实现单源与星族层面的贝叶斯证据与相变参数后验推断。
citation_leads: Phase transitions in neutron stars: “The order of a phase transition is defined by the lowest-order derivative of the free energy that is discontinuous as the system crosses the transition.”

Single-sources: “The data clearly distinguish individual curves, showing they prefer (more yellow colour) soft equations of state (i.e., with smaller radii at fixed mass) than stiff equations of state”

Populations: “If a universe has a true first-order phase transition (with relatively low transition density), then we will be able to definitively measure it with multiple neutron star mergers, and also get a handle on the density jump ratio parameter,”

Conclusions: “We performed synthetic injections into networks of both A+ and A$^\sharp$ observatories, showing that first-order phase transitions are recovered with $p(m=1)>0.9$ after about 14 events in both A+ and A$^\sharp$.”

analysis.title_zh: 利用色散量变化限制FRB的源运动速度
analysis.reason: 该工作直接关联 FRB 及其周围介质、致密天体中心引擎的出生反冲（natal kick）速度约束。文章建立了通过重复暴的色散量时变率 $d{\rm DM}/dt$ 分解并约束源径向速度 $v_r$ 与横向速度 $v_t$ 的理论方法，为检验 FRB 产生通道（如年轻大质量恒星超新星坍缩产生的高速中子星/磁星）提供了直接动力学工具。
analysis.result: 研究推导得出，源在周源介质中的运动可自然解释所观测到的 $d{\rm DM}/dt \sim 1\,{\rm pc\,cm^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$。当径向运动主导时，满足标度关系 $|d{\rm DM}/dt|=10^{-4}(|v_r|/100\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}})(\langle n_e \rangle/{\rm cm^{-3}})\,{\rm pc\,cm^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$；横向运动穿越柯尔莫哥洛夫湍流介质（$\beta=11/3$）引起的色散量均方根涨落标度为 $\sigma_{d{\rm DM}/dt} \approx [f_\beta {\rm SM}/2]^{1/2} v_t^{(\beta-2)/2}(\Delta t)^{(\beta/2)-2} \approx 3\times10^{-4} \left(\frac{\rm SM}{10^{-4}\ {\rm kpc\ m^{-20/3}}}\right)^{1/2}\left(\frac{v_t}{100\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}}\right)^{5/6}\left(\frac{\Delta t}{\rm yr}\right)^{-1/6}\,{\rm pc\,cm^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$。基于自由-自由吸收光深度 $\tau_{\rm ff} < 1$ 限制介质密度，推导得出重复暴样本的最小空间速度 $|v_s| = (v_r^2 + v_t^2)^{1/2}$ 约为 $\gtrsim 20 - 2800\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$，与银河系年轻高速中子星和磁星的反冲速度吻合。
analysis.problem: 重复 FRB 观测中探测到显著的色散量时间变化（$d{\rm DM}/dt \gtrsim 1\,{\rm pc\,cm^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$），需要明确其是否由致密天体自身的高速空间运动（如出生反冲速度）穿过周围电离介质所致，并定量分离径向与横向速度分量。
analysis.method: 将源速度分解为径向分量 $v_r$ 和横向分量 $v_t$，构建了三种模型场景：Scenario A 考虑常密度介质中的纯径向运动；Scenario B 考虑柯尔莫哥洛夫湍流介质中的横向运动引起的散射与涨落；Scenario C 将变化分解为线性项与随机项 ${\rm DM}(\mathbf{v}) = {\rm DM}_{\rm lin}(v_r) + {\rm DM}_{\rm sto}(v_t)$。结合自由-自由吸收光深度 $\tau_{\rm ff}\approx 3.3\times10^{-7}T_4^{-1.35}\nu_{\rm GHz}^{-2.1}{\rm EM} < 1$ 与散射量上限约束电子密度 $\langle n_e \rangle$，进而反推出源速度分量下限。
assumptions: 观测到的色散量变化主要由 FRB 源在宿主星系或周源介质中的自身空间运动主导，而非由银河系星际介质或宇宙学膨胀引起
limits: 对于极端源（如 FRB 20190520B），纯径向运动推断的 $|v_r| \gtrsim 3\times 10^3\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$ 超出了已知致密天体的最大观测空间速度
citation_leads: Main: “The radial velocity $v_r$ is most sensitive to the mean electron density $\langle n_e \rangle$. This is because when radial motions dominate, then $d{\rm DM}/dt = \langle n_e \rangle v_r$ (Methods).”

Methods: “We first consider the simplest scenario in which the FRB source is moving at a velocity $\mathbf{v} = (v_r,v_t)$ within a medium of constant mean density $\langle n_e \rangle$. The resulting $\Delta \DM(t)$ is entirely due to the changing”

Methods: “One way to evaluate whether transverse motion through turbulent density fluctuations dominate the observed $\DM(t)$ is to compare $|d\DM/dt|$ to the $\sigma_{d\DM/dt}$ expected for a turbulent medium”
analysis.research_progress: 建立了利用高时间分辨率色散量变化率 $d{\rm DM}/dt$ 与湍流涨落 $\sigma_{d{\rm DM}/dt}$ 联合限制致密天体空间反冲速度的方法，并将速度下限约束在 $\sim 20 - 2800\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$，支持 FRB 来自具有大出生反冲的大质量恒星核坍缩产物（年轻中子星/磁星）。

analysis.title_zh: SN 2023iop：一颗极端的类 SN 1987A 超新星与超大质量恒星的终结
analysis.reason: 该工作详细分析了目前已知光度最高、演化最极端的类 SN 1987A 超新星 SN 2023iop（峰值 $M_r \approx -20.14~\mathrm{mag}$，全波段辐射能量 $E_{\rm rad} \approx 4.3 \times 10^{50}~\mathrm{erg}$）。其极长上升时标（$\gtrsim 88$ 天）、巨大抛射物质量与 $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ 需求（$\approx 2.2~M_\odot$）以及晚期证认出的稳定 $[\mathrm{Ni\;II}]\,\lambda 7378$（对应 $^{58}\mathrm{Ni} \approx 0.02~M_\odot$），直接挑战了传统中微子驱动核塌缩机制，并为极高质量恒星（$\sim 190~M_\odot$）在贫金属环境下发生对不稳定性超新星（PISN）爆发结合星周介质（CSM）相互作用提供了罕见而关键的观测判例。
analysis.result: 测得该源峰值测辐射热光度为 $L_{\rm bol} = (4.0 \pm 1.0) \times 10^{43}~\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$，全波段积分总辐射能量达 $E_{\rm rad} = (4.3 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{50}~\mathrm{erg}$。由有效光球上升时标 $t_{\rm rise} \gtrsim 88$ 天导出抛射物质量下限 $M_{\rm ej} > 12~M_\odot$；峰值光度需要产生放射性镍质量 $M_{\rm ^{56}Ni} \approx 2.2~M_\odot$。在静止系波长 $5800\text{--}6200~\text{Å}$ 与 $7400\text{--}7800~\text{Å}$ 测得反方差加权平均连续谱线偏振度为 $P = 0.81 \pm 0.08\%$，揭示显著的非球对称几何。晚期 $+326$ 天测得 $[\mathrm{O\;I}]\,\lambda\lambda6300,6364$ 双线通量比 $F_{6300}/F_{6364} \approx 2.3$，处于光学薄与光学厚过渡态。多波段限制给出自由-自由吸收光深遵从标度律 $\tau_{\rm ff} \propto \nu^{-2.1}\,t^{-5}$，深埋中心引擎与 CSM 早期信号受阻碍。联合辐射模型指示其前身星符合 $190~M_\odot$ 的富氢 PISN 模型，晚期平台期辐射由隐蔽或非球对称 CSM 相互作用主导。
analysis.problem: SN 2023iop 具有长达 $\gtrsim 88$ 天的缓慢上升以及高达 $M_r \approx -20.14~\mathrm{mag}$ 的绝对星等，进入富氢超亮超新星（H-rich SLSN）能区。传统中微子驱动核塌缩模型能产生的动能（$\lesssim 2\times 10^{51}~\mathrm{erg}$）和 $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ 质量极限（$\lesssim 0.3~M_\odot$）完全无法解释其高达 $4.3\times 10^{50}~\mathrm{erg}$ 的辐射能量与峰值光度；而在光谱未见经典窄发射线与近紫外过剩的条件下，如何协调极高镍产额、超大抛射物质量、长时间维持的光球相与晚期极其平缓的衰减，构成了核心物理疑难。
analysis.method: 利用全天巡天（ZTF、ATLAS）及多台地面望远镜（VLT、Keck、LBT、LT、NOT、MMT 等）获取覆盖爆发前 $-51.4$ 天至 $+623.8$ 天的多波段测光、高低分辨率光谱及分光偏振（VLT/FORS2）数据。测光采用 AutoPhOT、SFFT 和 HOTPANTS 减算与动态分箱；光谱使用 PypeIt 等流程并严格与多波段测光进行绝对通量定标；结合黑体辐射演化、解析扩散时标标度律（$t_{\rm d} \approx [2\kappa M_{\rm ej}/(\beta c v)]^{1/2}$）、星云相禁线（$[\mathrm{O\;I}]$、$[\mathrm{Ni\;II}]$）光学薄/厚跃迁解析模型、PISN 网格数值模型（如 R190NL）、回落吸积供能模型（$\dot{E}_{\rm acc} = \eta \dot{M} c^2, \dot{M} \propto t^{-5/3}$）及非球对称 CSM 相互作用进行联合动力学与辐射拟合。
assumptions: 在通过光变衰变尾估计镍质量上限时，假设爆炸后晚期星云相能量完全由放射性 $^{56}\mathrm{Co} \to {}^{56}\mathrm{Fe}$ 衰变释放的 $\gamma$ 射线完全热化俘获驱动。
假设无偏振波段（5800–6200 Å 及 7400–7800 Å）测得的偏振主要反映超新星连续谱本征不对称性，而非宿主星系星际偏振（ISP）。
limits: 早期 Swift XRT（$L_{\rm X} < 4\times 10^{42}~\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$）与 AMI-LA 射电（$L_\nu < 4.4\times 10^{28}~\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$）上限由于致密抛射物内部巨大的束缚-自由和自由-自由吸收光深（$\tau_{\rm ff} \propto \nu^{-2.1} t^{-5}$），无法严格排除致密中心引擎或紧邻星周相互作用。

Results: “In the 5800--6200~\AA\ (rest frame) interval we measure $P=0.83\pm0.09~\%$, while in the 7400--7800~\AA\ region we find $P=0.76\pm0.14~\%$. The inverse‑variance‑weighted mean of these wavelength intervals is $P=0.81\pm0.08~\%$.”

The peak luminosity requires $\approx2.2~M_\odot$ of $^{56}$Ni, compatible with the tail-based upper limit and with the yield from the”

analysis.title_zh: 暗能量巡天（DES）中的核心坍缩超新星发生率
analysis.reason: 该工作利用 DES 5年观测样本精确测定了 $0 < z < 1.3$ 范围内的核心坍缩超新星（CC SN）体积发生率演化及剥离包层（SE SNe）占比，对超新星中心引擎宿主环境、前身星演化通道（双星 vs 单星风）以及宇宙恒星形成历史（CSFH）提供了重要限制。
analysis.result: 测得 CC SN 体积发生率满足幂律演化 $R_{\mathrm{CC}}(z) = R_0 (1 + z)^{\alpha}$，其中 $R_0 = (1.58 \pm 0.17) \times 10^{-4}\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}\,Mpc^{-3}}$，$\alpha = 2.85 \pm 0.25$。经验产额为 $k_{\mathrm{CC(MC)}} = 0.0114 \pm 0.0009\,M_\odot^{-1}$，与 Baldry & Glazebrook (2003) IMF 产额（$k_{\mathrm{BG03}} = 0.0116\,M_\odot^{-1}$）高度吻合，但比标准 Salpeter IMF 预测高约 $70\%$。剥离包层超新星占比线性拟合为 $f_{\mathrm{SE}}(z) = m z + c$，截距 $c = 0.31 \pm 0.05$（局域占比 $31 \pm 5\%$），斜率 $m = -0.01 \pm 0.09$，在 $0 < z < 1.3$ 范围内无显著演化，强烈支持双星剥离通道。
analysis.problem: 高红移 CC SNe 样本匮乏导致体积发生率演化测定存在大不确定性，且以往观测到的超新星发生率与根据标准 Salpeter IMF 导出的宇宙恒星形成历史（CSFH）预测存在差异（所谓的超新星遗漏或 IMF 差异问题）；同时剥离包层超新星（SE SNe）前身星主要来源于单星星风剥离还是双星相互作用仍存争议。
analysis.method: 利用 DES 5年巡天构建了两阶段 Random Forest 机器学习分类器筛选 CC SNe，并采用 13 个红移间隔独立分类；采用偏正态分布进行 $5 \times 10^4$ 次蒙特卡洛（MC）抽样以严格传播红移、消光、分类与探测效率非对称误差；通过前向物理模型卷积光度函数计算探测效率并反演体积发生率：$R_\mathrm{CC}(\langle z \rangle_i) = N_\mathrm{CC}(z_i) / [\epsilon_\mathrm{class}(z_i)\,\epsilon_\mathrm{detect}(z_i)\,V(z_i)\,T_\mathrm{rest}^{\mathrm{control}}(z_i)]$。
assumptions: 假定体积发生率与宇宙恒星形成率密度之间呈瞬时正比示踪关系：$R_{\mathrm{CC}}(z) = k\,\psi(z)$
limits: SE SNe 在低红移（$z<0.25$）存在约 $25\%$ 的分类不足，依赖经验常数校正乘子（1.33）外推至高红移
citation_leads: Introduction: “Over its five-year campaign (2013–2017), the Dark Energy Survey (DES) supernova (SN) survey recorded 31,636 light curves. Using a custom-built, two-stage random forest classifier, we identified 2,445 likely core-collapse SNe (CC SNe)”

Intoduction: “By utilizing 11 independent redshift bins to trace the rate evolution continuously from $0 < z < 1.3$, this work provides an unprecedentedly granular mapping of the cosmic CC SN rate across nine billion years of lookback time”

Selection & Classification: “To correct this bias, we apply an SE-specific calibration. The calibrated SE counts ($N_{\text{SE, cal}}$) are obtained by multiplying the uncalibrated counts by an under-classification correction factor of $1/0.75 \approx 1.33$.”

Rates, Detection Efficiency & Uncertainties: “The fiducial MC fitting approach implies a local SE fraction of $31 \pm 5$ per cent. The fitted slope is consistent with zero at the $0.1\sigma$ level, indicating no statistically significant evolution of the SE fraction with redshift”

Rates, Detection Efficiency & Uncertainties: “The total uncertainty on $R_\mathrm{CC}$ combines five contributions: Poisson counting statistics, classification corrections, detection efficiency, MC redshift propagation, and extinction corrections.”
Discussion: “the volumetric CC~SN rate, $R_{\mathrm{CC}}(z)$, closely traces the instantaneous star formation rate density, $\psi(z)$.”

Conclusions: “Within this range, the DES CC~SN rates are well fit by a power law of the form $R_{\mathrm{CC}}(z) = R_0 (1 + z)^{\alpha}$, with $R_0 = (1.58 \pm 0.17) \times 10^{-4}\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}\,Mpc^{-3}}$ and $\alpha = 2.85 \pm 0.25$.”
analysis.research_progress: 提供了目前在 $z=0\text{--}1.3$（回溯时间约 90 亿年）内空间分辨率最高、包含 11 个独立红移箱的连续 CC SN 体积发生率高精度测量，明确给出了红移幂律增长指数 $\alpha = 2.85 \pm 0.25$ 并证实 SE SN 比例恒定为 $31 \pm 5\%$。
